newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures bore the brunt of the franc slide early on Friday but soon regained their composure and moved back in step with the Bund market to end the week a fraction higher than they were last Friday.

The 10-year spread between French and government bonds suffered initially but then moved back to parity, unchanged from Thursday evening. The Treasury sold another 2.525 billion francs of BTANs taking the total amount sold to 20.183 this week.
Futures traders said the market felt "toppish" and unless the Bund managed to break through the 101.30 zone the French market risked being vulnerable to any strong German data.
One said all the good news was already priced into European bond markets and any extra impetus would have to come from the United States.
The December future settled at 127.74, up 0.10, from Thursday and up 0.12 from last Friday's settlement price but down from the contract high of 128.14 reached on Wednesday.
During Friday's session the contract failed to break convincingly through 127.80 but found good support at 127.34 which held soon after the open.

PIBOR contracts also came under heavy selling pressure early on Friday after the overnight franc slide. The March contract fell as much as 15 basis points but scrambled higher as the franc broke above resistance above 3.39 per mark.

Traders and analysts said while franc weakness could exacerbate the Bank of France's reluctance to narrow the gap between French and German interest rates quickly, there was no real danger of rates being raised to protect the currency.
"Mark/Paris might rise in the short-term but there's no question the Bank of France will raise rates," said a trader at a U.S. house.
Third quarter gross domestic product, due on Thursday, was expected to show a sharp 0.9 rise after a 0.4 percent drop in the second quarter, according to a Reuter poll.
